# 어둠을 건너 스스로 빛이 된 공주
# SET 05 — 신이 되어 돌아오다
# CUT 01 — 금빛 광휘 속 신격의 등장 / THE DEIFIED FIGURE EMERGING INTO GOLDEN RADIANCE
# Model: Suji / Shooting Date: 2026.08.09
# Vertical 3:4 / Person-Reference Image Mode
# Editorial Direction: Fusion Historical Fantasy K-Drama × Korean Myth Reinterpretation × Luminous Deification Fashion Editorial
# Primary Emotional Medium: Light and Reflection
# Core Motif: Suji appearing at the entrance of a golden glass corridor while sunrise reflections expand around her without overpowering her face
# Emotional Direction: Completed self-possession, quiet authority and the first appearance of someone who no longer needs external recognition

## 0) Reference Facial Identity, Target Hair, Body and Makeup Priority
The person in the attached reference image portrays Suji. Treat the attached reference image as the sole facial identity source. Preserve the exact same recognizable person, including her actual facial proportions, eye shape and spacing, eyebrows, nose, lips, cheek structure, jawline, skin tone, apparent adult age, natural asymmetry, beauty marks, hairline and all distinctive identity cues. Do not reconstruct her from a written Suji appearance, blend identities or create another woman. The name “Suji” defines only her narrative persona, controlled posture, emotional restraint, sophisticated styling direction and relationship with light and reflection. The hairstyle and makeup visible in the reference image are not fixed identity constraints.

MANDATORY TARGET-HAIR OVERRIDE MODE: completely replace the hairstyle shown in the reference image. Use glossy dark-brown hair divided by a precise center part with no bangs. Create a refined braided crown by wrapping two controlled braids around the head following the natural hairline and skull curvature. The braids remain firmly attached to the head and do not float above it. Gather the remaining hair into a rounded low bun positioned at the lower back of the head. Keep the bun moderate in size and physically secured below the occipital curve rather than exaggerated into an oversized ceremonial shape. Leave only one or two extremely fine curved temple strands while keeping the forehead, eyebrows, eyes, nose, lips, neck and garment collar clearly visible. Place a narrow champagne-gold ceremonial headpiece over the braided crown. Attach varied small transparent glass beads irregularly along the braids. Every bead is physically connected to the hair and creates only localized reflections. The hair remains dark brown. Warm gold appears only as a directional sunrise rim and reflected highlight, never as full gold hair color. Do not retain the source hairstyle’s length, outer silhouette, parting, bangs, curls, ponytail, half-up structure or loose-hair arrangement. No bob, short hair, side part, dense fringe, high ponytail, loose braid, fully loose hair or oversized high bun.

Construct a realistic adult feminine body with balanced, naturally curvaceous proportions. Present a visibly fuller yet anatomically plausible bust, a defined waist and graceful hips. Express the fuller bust through natural body volume and believable curvature, tension and drape beneath securely closed ceremonial hanbok layers. Do not create cleavage, an open collar, exposed chest, transparent bodice, compressed anatomy or excessively enlarged breasts. Replace the source makeup with the target ceremonial makeup described below. Makeup remains surface color, texture, transparency, placement and reflection only. Do not change actual eye shape, nose, lips, jaw, face width or age impression.

## 1) Photographic Pipeline and Film Character
Photographed on Kodak Vision3 250D motion-picture film using a full-frame-equivalent cinematic camera system. Render radiant but controlled golden highlights, broad highlight latitude, refined warm skin tones, clean separation between warm highlights and neutral shadows, fine organic cinematic grain and smooth highlight roll-off. Maintain detail in the backlit glass, gold embroidery, ivory fabric and facial skin. Avoid oversaturated yellow, flat metallic gold skin, clipped white highlights, artificial HDR, synthetic glow, excessive lens flare and crispy digital sharpening.

## 2) Scene Concept and Narrative
After restoring life with the water she obtained, Suji does not return to her former identity as an abandoned princess or remain defined only by sacrifice. She stands at the threshold between the human world and the celestial realm as someone who crossed death and life by her own decision. Her authority is not expressed through an aggressive pose, throne or oversized crown. It is visible in her stable body axis, sustained gaze and the way light expands through the space around her.

## 3) Location, Time and Environment
Place Suji at the entrance of a mythic corridor connecting the terrestrial world to the celestial realm just after sunrise. The corridor begins on broad champagne-gold stone steps and continues between handmade glass pillars. Each glass pillar contains small internal bubbles, slight waves, irregular thickness and different refraction angles. They must not resemble transparent acrylic or perfect CGI cylinders. Use a mixture of brushed gold, aged champagne-gold and restrained platinum metal fittings. Below the corridor, small gold-white life lights move in slow wave-like patterns, suggesting restored life without forming literal human figures. A weak upward wind moves only the lower edges of the long robe, wide sleeves, hanging ornaments and small light particles. The braided crown and low bun remain stable.

## 4) Background and Reflective Elements
Use softly blurred fragments of gold glass and several differently sized light particles in the foreground. Keep them away from Suji’s eyes, nose, lips and jaw. Place Suji in the middle ground at the beginning of the corridor. In the distance, show luminous clouds, layered glass architecture and broken sunrise reflections. Include one thin gold mirror panel made from layered glass and metal. It creates only a partial angled reflection of Suji’s shoulder or garment, never a perfect duplicated face. Maintain progressive optical depth from the foreground glass to Suji, the first pillars, distant corridor and sunlit clouds.

## 5) Camera, Composition and Pose
Use a full-frame 35mm lens at approximately f/3.2. Frame a vertical 3:4 medium-long portrait from just below the knees to above the ceremonial headpiece. Position Suji at the corridor entrance without making her disproportionately large compared with the architecture. Turn her torso approximately 50 degrees away from the camera, then rotate her head back approximately 30 degrees toward the camera. Keep the full face and both eyes clearly readable. Do not create a full back view. Direct her gaze to a point approximately 5 cm left of the camera lens, producing an almost direct gaze without fully confronting the viewer. Place the left foot one natural step ahead while distributing most body weight securely through the right foot. Keep both knees anatomically aligned, the pelvis stable and the shoulders approximately level.

The right arm hangs naturally beside the body inside the wide ceremonial sleeve. Show a continuous anatomical path from the right shoulder through the upper arm, elbow and forearm to the wrist and visible fingertips. Do not allow the sleeve to become an empty floating tube. The right fingertips must emerge naturally from the sleeve opening, remain separated and follow the arm axis. The left arm bends slightly below the fuller bust. The left thumb and index finger lightly stabilize the gold goreum or fabric immediately beneath its knot at the upper waist. The remaining fingers stay softly curved and separated. The left hand does not pull the collar or open the garment.

## 6) Expression and Persona
Keep the upper eyelids comfortably open and the pupils steady. The eyebrows remain relaxed without lifting the inner corners. Keep the lips gently closed, jaw released and cheeks calm. The expression communicates that Suji knows exactly who she has become, even without a smile, approval or ceremonial announcement. Avoid anger, arrogant superiority, triumphant grin, wide-eyed wonder, tears or a blank mannequin expression.

## 7) Ceremonial Wardrobe and Fuller Body Silhouette
Dress Suji in the completed SET 05 ceremonial fusion hanbok. The inner jeogori is warm ivory silk with high opacity, fine weave and soft satin reflectance. The middle jeogori is champagne-gold jacquard woven with low-relief motifs of water ripples, seeds and small birds. The structured outer jeogori blends pearl gold and platinum tones while following the natural shoulder line without padding or exaggerated width. Maintain a traditional crossover collar with slightly increased width for ceremonial dignity. Add a narrow 3 mm platinum piping along the collar edge. Keep all layers securely overlapped and closed. The naturally fuller bust creates graceful, visibly feminine upper-torso volume beneath the layered jeogori. Show believable curved drape, subtle side-seam tension and small compression folds near the underarms. No cleavage or artificial central breast seam.

Use wide ceremonial sleeves descending near the knees when the arms are lowered. The exterior is champagne gold and the lining is warm ivory. The lining becomes visible only through natural arm movement. The gold silk goreum consists of two weighted ribbons decorated with small glass beads and platinum knot details. They hang downward according to gravity. Use a three-layer skirt: opaque ivory silk inner skirt, champagne-gold jacquard middle skirt and pearl-gold organza outer skirt. The outer skirt changes tonal density and sheen under light but never reveals the legs. Attach a long ivory-gold ceremonial robe physically at the rear shoulders and neck. It trails toward the floor with realistic weight, compression and contact folds. Add a circular platinum waist ornament surrounded by gold wave and seed pendants of varied lengths. Prevent the pendants from intersecting each other or the body. Use irregular gold-thread, platinum-thread and transparent-bead embroidery depicting life-water ripples, sprouting seeds and wing forms. Add short glass-drop earrings, a thin mixed platinum-and-gold neck ornament and ivory silk flower shoes with champagne-gold embroidery and platinum edging.

## 8) Makeup and Skin Texture
Apply restrained ceremonial makeup combining formal wedding-guest refinement with controlled golden-hour bronze tones. Use a neutral semi-matte base preserving realistic pores, fine vellus hair, subtle tonal variation and natural matte-to-satin transitions. Keep the eyebrows naturally groomed with individual hairs visible. Apply a thin diffusion of champagne bronze and soft taupe over the center and outer eyelids. Place extremely fine diamond shimmer only at the eyelid center. Use thin brown-black shading close to the lash roots and naturally separated lashes. Blend low-opacity coral bronze and muted rose blush toward the outer cheek area. Apply a very fine champagne highlight only to the upper cheekbone and nose bridge where facing the declared light. Use caramel rose or muted brick-rose satin lip color within the exact natural lip boundary, preserving the real cupid’s bow and vertical lip texture. No gold glitter, metallic skin, excessive bronzing, strong contour, enlarged eyes, overdrawn lips or reshaped facial anatomy.

## 9) Lighting and Reflection
Place the low sunrise behind Suji as the main backlight. The glass pillars refract small fragmented gold and platinum reflections onto the hair crown, garment edges, sleeves and nearby stone. Use ivory and champagne-gold bounce from below and in front of the camera to preserve the complete face, both eyes and natural skin color. Add a low-intensity platinum side fill from the glass at camera-left. The restored-life lights below create only a faint upward reflection beneath the jaw, on the hands and along the goreum. Create restrained rim light along the braided crown, jaw, neck, shoulders, wide sleeves, trailing robe and skirt edge. Do not turn the skin uniformly gold or orange.

## 10) Essential Direction and Physical Anchors
The attached reference remains the sole facial identity source. Replace the reference hairstyle completely with the specified center-parted braided crown and moderate low bun. Maintain a naturally fuller bust beneath securely closed ceremonial layers; no cleavage. The right hand must remain connected to a complete anatomical arm inside the wide sleeve. The left hand must contact only the fabric below the goreum knot without opening the collar. Maintain stable standing mechanics, believable ceremonial fabric weight, physically attached jewelry, controlled upward wind, handmade glass refraction, restrained lens bloom, floor contact shadows and progressive optical depth.

## 11) Watermark
Add a small subtle watermark text “ⓒyulim_mood” in the bottom-right corner. Use Helvetica Neue, thin or light weight, white, semi-transparent and softly blended with consistent frame margins.

## 12) Negative Prompt

Avoid skin blur, heavy halation, artificial HDR, aggressive sharpening, and uniformly lifted blacks.

1. Reference Identity and Hair

Use PERSON-REFERENCE IMAGE MODE. The adult woman in the designated person reference portrays Suji. Use that reference as the sole source of facial identity, preserving the same recognizable adult person, underlying skin tone, apparent age, natural asymmetry, and distinctive identity cues. Let the reference define facial features directly without written beauty-trait redesign. Suji's name defines emotional presence and styling direction only. Relight her naturally for this scene rather than copying the reference exposure or lighting.

Use REFERENCE-HAIR PRESERVE MODE. Preserve the reference-visible hair length, color, texture, curl pattern, parting, fringe, volume, tied or loose structure, and overall silhouette. Allow only slight movement caused by turning her head and natural contact with clothing. Do not introduce a new hairstyle, new tied structure, or hair accessories.

Apply the explicitly requested naturally fuller bust while maintaining plausible anatomy and otherwise preserving reference-visible body proportions. Do not infer exact body measurements or import another model's body description. Keep this adjustment independent of facial identity and express it through a properly fitted, fully opaque blouse.

2. Story and Expression

Create one cinematic photograph of a quiet interruption during an ordinary workday. Suji has finished filling a glass with iced water and has just lifted it slightly from the counter when she notices a familiar person at the pantry entrance. The water has stopped running. Her hand pauses near the countertop as her eyes reach the person first, followed by a small, slightly shy smile.

Place the camera at that person's position so her gaze meets the viewer directly. Show exactly one person. Do not include the unseen companion's face, shoulder, hand, silhouette, or reflection.

Her composed office manner briefly softens into unmistakable pleasure at seeing someone she likes. Relax the brow and jaw, let the lower eyelids rise subtly with the smile, and lift both mouth corners gently while the lips remain lightly closed. Preserve a spontaneous, restrained expression rather than surprise, a broad toothy grin, puffed cheeks, or a polished advertising smile. Her eyes and interrupted gesture carry the romance.

3. Setting and Spatial Arrangement

Set the scene in a fictional high-rise office pantry on a clear autumn afternoon, approximately 40–60 minutes before sunset. The air is clear and still, without smoke, mist, or visible volumetric light beams. Ceiling lights are off.

A west-facing floor-to-ceiling window with adjustable horizontal blinds occupies camera-left. Low sunlight enters obliquely, casting elongated bands across a stainless-steel island and the floor. Suji stands approximately one meter from the window at the camera-near short end of the island, beside a built-in chilled-water dispenser.

Position her beyond the island's near corner so the countertop does not conceal her waist, either hand, or the lower part of the glass. A thin diagonal counter edge enters the lower-left foreground and leads toward her hands and face.

Behind her, a transparent glass partition borders a passage into the office. Suggest distant desks through soft architectural shapes. Through the window, show overlapping city buildings without emphasizing a recognizable landmark. Keep strong background lines and bright patches away from her face and hairline.

4. Glass and Environmental Details

Include one clear faceted crystal highball glass, approximately 15 cm tall and narrow enough to hold comfortably. Give it recognizable flat facets and cut edges with realistic wall thickness. It must read as functional drinkware rather than an oversized gemstone.

Fill it approximately two-thirds with clear water. Exactly three irregularly oriented ice cubes float near the surface, mostly submerged, with small portions above the waterline. Add small, uneven condensation droplets to the exterior, partially wiped away where her fingers contact the lower glass. Include no straw, fruit, herb garnish, handle, or second glass.

Keep the dispenser visible only enough to establish her preceding action. There is no running stream; a few residual droplets remain on its drip tray.

The distant partition faintly reflects the window and bright architectural surfaces without producing a second recognizable face or person. The brushed stainless steel shows elongated, softened reflections following its grain rather than a mirror-sharp image of Suji.

5. Camera and Composition

Use a full-frame camera with a 50 mm lens, f/3.5, and a 1/200-second exposure, adjusting ISO for available window light. Compose a vertical 9:16 medium-long portrait from a small margin above her head to mid-thigh. Keep both hands and the entire glass inside the frame, avoiding crops through wrists, elbows, or knees.

Place the camera approximately at Suji's eye level, around 1.8–2 meters away, with the framing adjusted within that range to retain the intended crop. Keep the camera nearly level and architectural verticals stable. Position her slightly right of center, with her face near the upper third and window-lit negative space to the left.

Focus on her eyes while keeping the principal facial features readable. Hold the glass close to her body rather than extending it toward the lens, so its shape and hand contact remain legible. Let focus soften progressively behind her head and shoulders toward the partition and office. Avoid artificial portrait-mode cutouts, blurred facial features, and wide-angle facial distortion.

6. Body Position and Hand Contact

Keep her pelvis oriented toward the island while her upper torso turns approximately 25 degrees toward the camera. Her head turns a little farther to establish direct eye contact without excessive neck rotation. Lower both shoulders naturally. Her weight rests slightly more on the anatomical left foot, with the right foot half a step behind for balance; both feet remain grounded outside the crop. Do not arch her back, thrust her chest forward, or exaggerate the waist twist.

Her anatomical right hand holds the lower third of the glass. The thumb contacts one side, while the index, middle, and ring fingers curve naturally around the opposing facets. The little finger rests beside the ring finger and lightly supports the lower side. The visible fingers follow a believable grip and may be naturally occluded by the glass; do not force all five into full view.

Keep the right elbow loosely bent near her torso. The glass base hovers approximately 5 cm above the countertop, still over its edge area. The glass remains upright, with an approximately horizontal water surface and no spill.

Her anatomical left hand rests lightly on the counter edge after operating the dispenser. Keep its fingers gently separated and the wrist aligned with the forearm. Position this hand distinctly apart from the right hand and glass so both actions are readable. It makes light contact rather than carrying her body weight.

Maintain anatomically valid fingers, coherent glass refraction, and small contact shadows at finger-to-glass and hand-to-counter junctions. Fingers must not penetrate the glass or merge with each other.

7. Wardrobe and Fabric Behavior

Dress Suji in a pale-lavender silk-satin cowl-neck blouse and ivory high-waisted tailored trousers. The blouse is lightweight and fluid but fully opaque, including where illuminated by direct sunlight. Give it comfortable long sleeves, neatly closed cuffs, clean seams, and a moderately deep cowl neckline that folds softly across the upper chest.

Render a naturally fuller, softly rounded bust beneath the clothing with realistic gravity and discreet underlying support. Fit the blouse with sufficient fabric and shaping through the bust so fullness reads through its overall silhouette and gentle drape. Preserve comfortable ease across the chest and underarms. The fabric must not cling to each breast, create molded cup shapes, stretch into horizontal strain lines, or pull the neckline downward.

Keep the cowl's folds structurally separate from the body's contour: the neckline hangs from its shoulder attachments and finished facing, while the blouse body falls smoothly over the bust. Maintain modest upper-chest coverage as she turns, with no deep cleavage, exposed underwear, transparency, open side gaps, or distorted seams. Do not add buttons, a front opening, a corset, or a cutout.

Tuck the hem neatly into the trousers, leaving slight blousing above the waistband. Introduce modest diagonal folds at the rotating waist and short compression folds inside the bent right elbow. Silk highlights follow illuminated fold ridges rather than forming an artificial bright patch over the chest.

Use medium-weight wool-blend crepe for the ivory trousers, with opaque lining, a clean waistband, concealed front zipper and hook closure, one front pleat on each side, and a softly falling straight-leg cut. Preserve fabric ease around the pelvis and thighs rather than a tight fit. Retain visible texture and tonal separation in the ivory fabric.

The off-frame footwear is ivory low-heeled pointed pumps. Add only a pair of small silver stud earrings, without a necklace or large wrist accessories.

8. Makeup and Skin Rendering

Apply understated daily office makeup as surface color and finish without changing facial anatomy. Use a thin neutral skin tint matched to her underlying complexion and a soft satin finish. Retain subtle regional color variation and delicate natural skin texture appropriate to this camera distance.

Groom the brows while preserving visible hairs and their natural placement. Apply low-saturation neutral-brown eyeshadow with softly diffused boundaries, a fine brown line between the lashes, and lightly defined lashes without exaggerated length or density. Keep the under-eye area natural rather than heavily brightened.

Place a faint beige-peach blush toward the outer cheeks and a small amount of restrained sheen only on cheekbone areas that actually receive the window light. Use a translucent rose-beige tinted lip balm within the natural lip boundary. Do not enlarge the lips, reshape the eyes, narrow the face, or change her apparent age.

Avoid waxy smoothing, enlarged decorative pores, metallic highlights, self-luminous skin, or a separately brightened face.

9. Shared Window Lighting and Material Response

The primary light is low autumn sunlight entering from approximately 60 degrees to camera-left and forward of Suji, with a fictional solar elevation around 10–15 degrees. Direct-light edges are reasonably defined; broad sky illumination through the same window supplies weak diffuse ambient light.

Tilt the blinds and position Suji so a comparatively broad opening lights the face without narrow dark stripes crossing both eyes. Concentrate repeated light-and-shadow bands on the sleeves below shoulder height, the island, and the floor. Make this distribution consistent with the actual slats and her position.

Warm sunlight reaches the window-facing cheek, temple, side of the nose, and corresponding planes of the neck and hands. Keep the opposite cheek and underside of the jaw visibly darker, supported only by weak sky illumination and soft reflections from nearby light-colored walls. Maintain continuous exposure, color temperature, and shadow direction across face, neck, hands, and clothing.

The silk produces elongated, smooth specular accents along sun-facing cowl and sleeve folds. The wool-crepe trousers show broader, more matte illuminated planes. Brushed metal stretches reflections along its surface grain.

Place small, bright highlights on the illuminated glass edges and ice. Transmitted sunlight creates a restrained refracted light pattern on the nearby countertop on the side away from the sun, with faint spectral separation in only a small portion. The glass does not emit light, and no rainbow crosses the entire face.

The partition remains a passive reflector of the room rather than a separate key light. Use no frontal flash, portrait-specific fill light, added reflector, or uniform halo around the hair. Eye catchlights follow the real window position and eyelid occlusion rather than identical painted white dots.

Protect the brightest silk, glass, and ivory details while retaining natural darkness in the office background and on the shaded side of the face.

10. Essential Visual Anchors

Prioritize the direct, tender eye contact, the interrupted movement of a glass just above the counter, and the coherent afternoon light shared by skin, silk, metal, and water. Keep the right hand supporting the glass and the left hand resting separately on the counter. The dispenser has already stopped.

Maintain the same recognizable facial identity from the designated reference. Preserve believable fabric weight, pose-dependent compression and folds, natural contact shadows, coherent perspective, progressive optical depth, hair gravity, and physically consistent reflection and refraction.

Avoid additional people, duplicate reflections, extra glasses, fused or extra fingers, hands passing through glass, running water, spilled water, distorted garment construction, artificial chest emphasis, mismatched face lighting, and a flat synthetic background.

11. Watermark

Add the exact text “ⓒyulim_mood” as a fixed graphic overlay at the bottom center. Use clean white at moderate opacity in an elegant high-contrast calligraphic italic signature style, with thin hairlines, thicker downstrokes, connected lowercase letters, and a pronounced rightward slant.

Keep the complete signature approximately 23–25% of the canvas width and 4–5% of its height, horizontally centered, with its lowest stroke 2.5% above the bottom edge. Preserve the underscore and every character clearly, with all flourishes inside the frame. Attach “ⓒ” directly to “yulim_mood” without a space.

Do not add outlines, shadows, glow, boxes, borders, or background plaques. Treat the signature as typography rather than a light source. Print no title, date, model name, or cut number in the image.

# Single-Cut Prompt — The Last Man Left Behind

## Character Identity Declaration

Taegun is a **one-off fictional Korean middle-aged male character created exclusively for this single image**.

He is not Yulim, Arin, Suji, Hayoon, Seorin, Jieun, or any other registered recurring character.

Do not borrow, blend or inherit any registered character’s:

* facial identity
* body proportions
* hairstyle
* profession
* emotional persona
* visual mood system
* wardrobe language
* established narrative world

Create Taegun only from the physical and emotional description written in this prompt.

The submerged adult son is also a one-off supporting character. His face must remain secondary, partially obscured by water refraction and not developed into a distinct recurring identity.

---

## 1) Film Reference and Color Palette

Create an ultra-realistic vertical 3:4 cinematic action-drama photograph captured with the visual characteristics of **Kodak Vision3 500T 35mm motion-picture film, exposed around EI 400**.

The frame must resemble a difficult practical film shot captured at the climax of a grounded historical action drama, not a fantasy character illustration, game concept art, comic panel or glossy hero poster.

Kodak Vision3 500T must define the image through:

* violent concentrated golden backlight
* cold cyan and cobalt underwater shadows
* deep but readable forest-green blacks
* restrained dark blood-red accents
* compressed luminous highlights
* broad cinematic dynamic range
* fine organic 35mm grain
* subtle halation around hard backlight
* restrained micro-contrast
* low-saturation weathered skin
* smooth highlight rolloff
* subtle analog density variation
* strong but believable warm–cool separation
* slightly softened optical edges
* realistic atmospheric depth

Divide the image naturally into two connected color environments.

The upper 65–70% of the frame represents the collapsing bridge and Taegun’s remaining world:

* burning pale-gold dawn backlight
* near-white overexposed sky around the mountain ridge
* dark forest-green fabric
* weathered charcoal stone
* muted ivory bandages
* restrained dark crimson blood
* wind-driven dust and debris

The lower 25–30% represents the submerged son’s escape route:

* deep cobalt blue water
* cyan-green surface reflections
* pale desaturated underwater skin
* blackened depth
* narrow streaks of refracted light
* small irregular air bubbles

Do not create a graphic split screen, collage, diptych or visible dividing line.

Connect the two environments through the actual geometry of the broken stone bridge, the dark water surface, reflected shadows and realistic optical refraction.

Red must remain limited to three controlled visual points:

1. blood at Taegun’s mouth and chin
2. the old dark-crimson knot attached to his coat
3. a small severed fragment of crimson cord sinking toward the son

Do not spread bright red throughout the image.

The three red accents should form a subtle visual path between father and son.

---

## 2) Scene Concept and Story

At the final moment of a violent confrontation, an ancient stone bridge crossing a deep mountain gorge has collapsed across more than half of its span.

Taegun has deliberately dropped his critically injured adult son into the river below.

This was not an attack.

The fast current connects to a hidden water passage farther downstream and offers the son the only remaining route of escape from the enemies surrounding the bridge.

The son has sunk beneath the surface and is beginning to orient his body toward the brighter underwater passage.

His forearms and wrists are wrapped in damaged cloth bandages.

One hand reaches upward through the distorted blue water, but Taegun does not reach back.

Taegun understands that looking toward the water or extending his hand would reveal his son’s position.

Instead, he rotates away from the gorge and turns toward the approaching enemies.

He is severely wounded.

Blood runs from the corner of his mouth.

One eye is swollen.

His posture is beginning to fail.

Standing upright is already physically difficult.

Even so, he forces himself to laugh at the enemies moving toward him.

The laugh is not pleasure, insanity or confidence in victory.

It is an intentionally exaggerated provocation designed to hold every hostile eye on him until his son has travelled far enough through the water.

### Narrative Anchor

**To buy his son enough time to survive, the father lies to his enemies by pretending that he is still impossible to defeat.**

The emotional sequence must be readable within one frame:

1. Taegun is mortally wounded.
2. His adult son is escaping underwater.
3. Taegun refuses to look back.
4. He turns toward the enemy and laughs more violently.
5. The viewer gradually understands that the laugh is a concealed farewell rather than a declaration of victory.

The emotional language is:

* savage paternal protection
* defiant sacrifice
* concealed farewell
* pain converted into intimidation
* love expressed through refusal to look back
* the final lie of an exhausted father
* fear hidden beneath aggression
* momentary relief buried inside physical agony

Do not idealize Taegun as a fearless legendary warrior.

Fear, pain and exhaustion must remain visible beneath the expression he is forcing himself to perform.

---

## 3) Location, Time and Environment

### Location

An ancient stone bridge crossing a deep mountain gorge with a violent dark river below.

The bridge’s central span has collapsed due to combat and structural damage.

The remaining edge contains:

* irregular fractured stone blocks
* broken timber reinforcement
* torn hemp ropes
* unstable rubble
* shattered parapet sections
* damp moss trapped in stone joints
* dust falling from fresh cracks
* small fragments vibrating near the edge

The water below is deep and fast-moving.

Farther from the darkest section, a faintly brighter underwater route suggests the entrance to a concealed natural tunnel.

The tunnel must not glow magically.

It is only slightly brighter because pale dawn light reaches that section through an opening in the gorge.

### Season

**Late autumn transitioning into early winter.**

Most leaves have already fallen.

The mountain vegetation is sparse, dark and wind-stripped.

There is no snowfall.

Use the following environmental particles instead:

* dry irregular leaf fragments
* stone dust
* broken crimson cord fibers
* tiny blood-mixed droplets
* splintered wood fragments
* faint river mist
* scattered grit from the collapsing bridge

### Time of Day

**Very early dawn, immediately as the sun begins rising behind the mountain ridge.**

The solar disc must not be directly visible.

A narrow gap between mountain slopes allows concentrated golden light to burst from behind Taegun.

The bridge and Taegun receive intense low-angle backlight, while the submerged area remains predominantly dark blue.

### Wind Direction

A strong crosswind moves from the rear-right of the image toward the front-left.

The following elements must respond to exactly the same wind direction:

* Taegun’s long silver-white hair
* the broad collar and lower panels of his coat
* the crimson knot and tassel
* dry leaves
* stone dust
* small airborne droplets
* fine loose rope fibers

The son is underwater and must not be affected by this wind.

The underwater current travels separately from the lower-left toward the upper-right.

The son’s:

* wet hair
* loose bandage ends
* fabric edges
* bubbles
* small crimson cord fragment

must follow the underwater current rather than the atmospheric wind.

The opposing directions of wind and water should suggest that father and son have already entered two separate physical worlds.

---

## 4) Background Layers and Props

### Foreground Layer

Place a limited number of close, heavily defocused elements near the lens:

* a dark out-of-focus fragment of enemy clothing
* dust turning pale gold in the backlight
* two or three small dark-red droplets
* a broken rope crossing one corner diagonally
* tiny illuminated fibers and grit

Foreground elements must not cover:

* Taegun’s clearly visible eye
* his mouth
* the crimson knot
* his rope-holding hand
* the submerged son’s reaching hand

Do not create an excessively busy debris storm.

### Midground Layer

Taegun’s face and upper body dominate the central and upper part of the image.

He stands at the fractured edge of the bridge.

His pelvis and lower torso remain oriented toward the water where he has just released his son.

His rib cage, shoulders, neck and face have rotated abruptly toward the enemies approaching from behind.

His coat and hair lag fractionally behind the body rotation, creating believable secondary motion.

Taegun’s raised left arm occupies the upper-left area of the composition.

His left hand grips a thick hemp rope connected to unstable bridge debris.

The rope is supporting part of the damaged remaining structure.

Releasing it would cause the remaining bridge section to collapse and obstruct the enemy’s advance.

### Underwater Lower Layer

Show the adult son beneath the water in the lower 25–30% of the frame.

Do not present him as a separate portrait.

Reveal only:

* a partially distorted side-face silhouette
* open eyes directed upward
* short dark wet hair
* bandaged forearms
* one upward-reaching hand
* a lean shoulder and partial upper torso
* small irregular bubbles
* fabric moving with the underwater current

The son must be considerably smaller than Taegun.

The viewer should notice Taegun first and discover the son only after examining the lower portion of the image.

### Distant Background

Include:

* a mountain ridge dissolving into intense dawn light
* black conifer silhouettes moving in the wind
* the fractured far end of the bridge
* long indistinct enemy shadows
* blurred weapon silhouettes
* dust displaced by approaching movement
* river spray and low dawn mist

Do not clearly depict enemy faces.

The enemies should exist through:

* elongated shadows
* partial weapons
* vague human movement inside dust
* pressure and directional threat outside the frame

They must not become competing main characters.

---

### Prop 1 — Tensioned Hemp Rope

Taegun’s left hand grips a thick, damaged hemp rope.

The rope must show:

* frayed hemp fibers
* irregular broken strands
* a blood-darkened grip area
* visible axial tension
* compressed fibers beneath the fingers
* tiny loose strands catching golden light
* believable strain between the hand and bridge debris

The rope must not hang loosely.

It carries both Taegun’s pulling force and the load of the unstable bridge structure.

Its tension must be physically obvious.

### Prop 2 — Old Crimson Family Knot

Attach an old crimson knotted cord to the shoulder and upper chest of Taegun’s dark-green coat.

The knot has:

* dark crimson silk cord
* irregular handmade construction
* faded and dirty sections
* frayed tassel ends
* blood and rain stains
* wind-driven directional movement
* one severed missing section

It must not resemble luxurious royal decoration.

It should feel like a small family marker Taegun has carried for many years.

A severed fragment of the same cord is falling into the water and drifting toward the son.

### Prop 3 — Shared Bandaging Habit

Both father and son have cloth wraps around their wrists, suggesting a practical habit passed between them.

The wraps are similar in method but not identical props.

Taegun’s wraps:

* dirty ivory cloth
* blood-darkened knuckles
* partially loosened layers
* strong compression around the wrist
* irregular staining and frayed edges

The son’s wraps:

* pale gray-blue underwater coloration
* floating loose ends
* trapped miniature bubbles
* softened edges caused by water refraction
* minimal visible blood

---

## 5) Camera Composition and Body Mechanics

### Aspect Ratio

**Vertical 3:4 composition.**

### Framing

Taegun’s face and upper body occupy approximately 65–70% of the upper and central frame.

The submerged son occupies approximately 25–30% of the lower frame.

The boundary between the two spaces is formed naturally by:

* the bridge edge
* dark water reflection
* mist
* surface refraction
* shadow from the collapsed structure

No artificial frame division.

### Camera Specification

* large-format digital cinema sensor
* 50mm prime lens
* aperture f/2.8
* shutter speed 1/640 sec
* ISO 800
* exposure compensation around –0.3 EV
* Kodak Vision3 500T 35mm emulation
* subtle practical lens halation
* physically accurate depth of field
* restrained optical bloom

The fast shutter should sharply preserve Taegun’s visible eye, facial structure and rope hand.

Allow only a very short directional motion trace on:

* hair tips
* tassel fibers
* dust
* small droplets
* loose coat edges

Do not blur the entire image.

### Camera Position

Place the camera approximately **30–40° behind Taegun’s shoulder line**, capturing the instant he rotates toward the enemy.

The camera sits slightly below Taegun’s chest level with a restrained **5–8° low angle**.

Avoid an extreme heroic low angle.

The viewpoint should subtly resemble the final upward view the son might have through the water, while still remaining physically outside or immediately above the waterline.

### Taegun’s Gaze

**Taegun does not look into the camera.**

He looks slightly to camera-right toward the approaching enemy outside the frame.

He must not look downward toward his son.

One eye may be partially obscured by shadow, swelling or windblown hair.

The other eye must remain clearly visible and sharply focused.

### Son’s Gaze

The son looks upward toward Taegun through the distorted water surface.

Their eyes do not meet directly.

Their gaze directions should form a broken diagonal relationship rather than mutual eye contact.

### Taegun’s Full Pose

* left foot planted on a stable interior stone block
* right foot angled near the fractured bridge edge
* pelvis oriented toward the river
* rib cage rotated approximately 60° toward the enemy
* left shoulder elevated by rope tension
* right shoulder dropped and weakened
* neck strongly rotated without excessive backward extension
* chin slightly raised but not posed triumphantly
* upper body beginning to collapse subtly forward
* core tension uneven due to injury
* weight distributed primarily through the left leg
* knees not locked straight
* boots maintaining believable stone contact

### Left Hand and Rope Contact

The raised left hand grips the rope with precise anatomy:

* thumb wraps beneath and around the rope
* index and middle fingers provide the strongest compression
* ring finger and little finger separate slightly under strain
* palm remains fully engaged with the rope
* hemp fibers visibly compress between the fingers
* wrist stays aligned with the forearm
* knuckles show tension without anatomical distortion
* a clear contact shadow appears between hand and rope
* no rope passing through the palm
* no fingers hidden in impossible overlaps

### Right Hand

Taegun carries no weapon in his right hand.

The right hand has just moved away from pressing his wounded side.

Show:

* dark blood across the palm
* fingers not fully extended
* index and middle fingers hanging slightly lower
* weakened wrist
* mild involuntary tremor implied by posture
* clear visual separation from the coat
* realistic blood transfer where the palm touched the garment

Do not merge the hand with the fabric.

Do not add a sword, dagger, firearm or supernatural object.

---

## 6) Character Appearance

### Taegun — One-Off Middle-Aged Male Character

Create a Korean man in his late forties to early fifties with an entirely original identity developed only for this image.

His appearance:

* large weathered facial structure
* broad cheekbones
* strong angular jaw
* deep-set gray-brown eyes
* heavy straight eyebrows
* long silver-white hair extending past the shoulders
* irregular swept-back hair with uncontrolled volume
* coarse short stubble along the jaw and upper lip
* visible forehead lines
* an old scar near one eyebrow
* another faint scar across one cheek
* broad neck
* powerful shoulders and upper body
* physically strong frame
* visible exhaustion and blood loss
* intimidating exterior
* deeply protective emotional interior

Do not beautify him into a young fantasy prince.

Do not give him the face of a clean K-pop idol, fashion model or polished historical-drama aristocrat.

He must look like someone whose physical history has accumulated across his face, hands, posture and clothing.

### Skin Texture

* restrained retouching
* subtle tonal variation
* delicate natural texture
* visible pores
* coarse stubble
* sweat mixed with dust
* irregular bruising around one eye
* small cuts across cheek and brow
* dried and fresh blood at the mouth
* realistic pallor caused by blood loss
* uneven skin temperature
* no smooth beauty-filter finish
* no polished heroic complexion

### Hair

Long, rough silver-white hair with mixed natural tones:

* gray
* aged ivory
* faded beige
* muted silver
* slightly darker sweat-soaked roots

Only the backlit outer edges should appear bright gold-white.

Hair behavior:

* dense layered strands
* uneven broken ends
* asymmetrical mass
* strong single-direction wind movement
* individual strands crossing the forehead and cheek
* compressed damp strands near the temples
* no perfect fantasy mane
* no symmetrical salon waves
* no clean center part

### Wardrobe

Taegun wears a long dark forest-green combat coat constructed from heavy woven wool and weathered cotton.

The coat includes:

* broad folded collar
* dark forest-green coloration
* faded seam edges
* torn right shoulder
* blood-darkened side panel
* embedded dust
* irregular wind-driven folds
* heavy physical drape
* old crimson knotted cords at shoulder and chest
* partially exposed off-white inner collar

Under the coat, he wears a rough gray-white cotton shirt.

The shirt has:

* an open and damaged neckline
* sweat-darkened cloth
* blood staining
* fabric adhering slightly to the upper chest
* compression and wrinkles caused by torso rotation
* no intentional sensual exposure

### Expression

The expression combines three simultaneous emotional forces:

1. an exaggerated laugh created to intimidate the enemy
2. genuine pain from severe injury
3. brief hidden relief that the son is still moving away

At first glance, the viewer may interpret him as laughing violently.

On closer inspection, the viewer should realize that he is using the laugh to prevent himself from looking back or breaking emotionally.

#### Eyes

* one eye opened wide and locked onto the enemy
* the swollen eye unable to open completely
* pupils tracking a precise off-screen threat
* inner eyebrows pulled downward
* lower eyelids carrying fatigue
* pain visible in the muscles beneath the eyes
* no visible tears
* no sentimental upward gaze

#### Mouth

* mouth open between a laugh and a battle shout
* several upper and lower teeth naturally visible
* one side of the mouth raised asymmetrically due to injury
* a small amount of blood running from the corner of the lips toward the chin
* realistic dark oral cavity
* no excessive emphasis on tongue or teeth
* no horror-style mouth distortion

#### Facial Muscles

* deep vertical tension between the eyebrows
* contracted muscles beside the nose
* tightened cheek muscles
* strong jaw tension
* one cheek trembling slightly from pain
* asymmetrical tension caused by swelling and injury

### Adult Son — Supporting Character

The son is an adult Korean man in his early to mid-twenties.

He has:

* short dark wet hair
* lean athletic build
* youthful but bruised face
* bandaged hands and forearms
* pale desaturated underwater skin
* open eyes looking upward
* lips slightly parted
* a small irregular stream of bubbles

Keep his face partially indistinct.

Water refraction, surface movement and depth of field should obscure exact facial identity while preserving the emotional readability of his gaze and reaching hand.

---

## 7) Lighting, Color and Atmosphere

### Main Light Above Water

Use a concentrated low golden dawn backlight entering from behind Taegun on image-right.

The light source sits approximately **5–10° above the horizon** behind the mountain ridge.

It should feel harsher and more directional than a soft romantic sunrise because it passes through a narrow opening between the mountains.

### Golden Rim Light Areas

Apply controlled golden rim light to:

* outer perimeter of Taegun’s silver hair

She has stopped naturally after walking, with one foot still half a step ahead. An antique gold pocket watch hangs loosely from one lowered hand, while her other arm rests naturally beside her body. ## 3) Location, Time, and Environment

The front terrace of the Orangery Palace in Potsdam, Germany, during a quiet early-summer morning between 8:10 and 9:10 a.m.

A quiet river embankment or open-field bicycle path outside the city, late summer turning toward early autumn. Yulim and her companion were riding home, saw an unusually clear Milky Way, and stopped without planning to. Late August to early September, approximately 22:30–00:30 after astronomical twilight. Moonless or very low-moon conditions; no visible moon or strong moonlight. Slightly cool, faintly humid air, little wind, clear sky.

Vertical 3:4, full-frame, approximately 24mm at f/1.8–2.0. Camera height 55–75cm above ground, optical axis tilted upward around 6–10°. The low viewpoint makes the sky enormous without distorting bodies.

Yulim turns her torso 20–30° toward the companion with relaxed shoulders. Her left leg supports most weight; the right knee bends gently and the right heel lifts only about 8–12cm from the grass. She keeps her own balance.

Yulim looks toward the companion's eyes or face. Upper eyelids are slightly relaxed, brows released, jaw and cheeks soft. Lips are closed or parted only 1–2mm. No obvious grin; only a faint softening at one corner. The feeling is “I wish this moment could last.”

# 2026.08.29 YULIM — RICHMOND PAINTED WEDDING PORTRAITS
# SET 03 / CUT 02 — THE BRIDE ALONE
# Vertical 3:4 / Person-Reference Image Mode — Face Identity Only
# Output Type: OIL-ON-CANVAS PAINTED PORTRAIT, NOT PHOTOGRAPHY
# Editorial Direction: Museum Bridal Portrait Editorial × Old Master Portrait Reinterpretation × European Aristocratic Interior Portrait × Modern Wedding Couture × Richmond Castle Interior Portrait Series × Painted Bridal Iconography

## 0) REFERENCE FACE IDENTITY

The woman in the attached person reference portrays Yulim.
Treat the reference image as the sole source of facial identity.

Preserve Yulim’s exact recognizable facial proportions, eye shape and spacing, eyebrows, nose, lips, cheeks, jawline, skin tone, apparent adult age, natural asymmetry, and distinctive identity cues.

Do not replace her with a generic idealized painted bride.
Do not redesign her from a written description.

The final face must remain recognizable as the reference person while being fully translated into the same oil-painted material as the rest of the portrait.

There must be no photographic face layer or digitally realistic skin patch.

## 1) TARGET-HAIR OVERRIDE MODE — BRIDAL LOW CHIGNON

Completely replace any conflicting source hairstyle.

Create dark-brown bridal hair with a soft center-to-6:4 part, no bangs, and naturally controlled crown volume.
Sweep both side sections backward while preserving a soft romantic surface rather than a rigid slicked style.

Gather the hair immediately above the nape into a low romantic chignon made from softly layered overlapping sections.
Keep one or two extremely fine face-framing strands near the ears.

Use only two or three small pearl pins or ivory floral pins asymmetrically in the chignon.

No loose long hair over the shoulders, no tiara, no crystal crown, and no exaggerated veil.

Preserve the same facial identity while changing only the hair and scene styling.

## 2) PAINTING MEDIUM · FACE MATERIAL CONTROL

Create an intimate museum-quality oil-on-canvas bridal portrait.

Use layered translucent glazing, softly blended midtone passages, visible refined brushwork, subtle canvas texture, restrained opaque highlights, and gentle varnished depth.

The complete image—face, hair, gown, hands, background, and frame—must be unified by one consistent oil-painted material language.

The face must read clearly as a painting not only from a normal viewing distance, but also when the image is enlarged.
The viewer should never feel that the face is still essentially a photograph.

Therefore:
- skin must be modeled with painterly tonal planes rather than photographic pore realism
- eyelids, under-eyes, nose bridge, nostrils, philtrum, and lips must show oil-painted interpretation
- the eyes must be readable but not lens-sharp or glassy
- the eyelashes must not become hyper-detailed photographic strands
- the lips must not appear like a beauty photo with digital gloss
- eyebrows must be painted with fine controlled strokes, not ultra-sharp hair-by-hair photography
- facial edges and transitions must remain softly brush-resolved

No photo-face plus painted-body hybrid.
No oil-filtered photograph.
No hyperreal digital painting.
No flat illustration.

## 3) COLOR PALETTE

Use a refined bridal portrait palette:
warm ivory,
pearl,
muted champagne,
old rose,
soft olive,
taupe,
shadowed stone,
antique gold,
low-saturation natural skin.

The mood is luminous, intimate, restrained, and timeless.

## 4) SCENE CONCEPT

Create an independent formal bridal portrait devoted only to Yulim.

This is not a crop from the couple portrait.
It is a separate official painted bridal image focused on Yulim’s face, neckline, hair, hands, and upper gown.

One-line narrative:
The marriage is remembered through a portrait devoted only to the bride herself.

## 5) LOCATION · BACKGROUND

Interior of Schloss Richmond.

Use a different visual zone from CUT 01, such as a quieter decorated wall or a position beside a tall window.

No foreground props.

Midground:
Yulim alone.

Background:
muted decorative plaster or painted wall, restrained olive-taupe shadow, and possibly a very soft drapery edge.

Keep the background quiet and secondary.

No chair.
No bouquet.
No visible groom.

## 6) CLASSICAL PORTRAIT FRAME

Surround the entire canvas with a believable carved gilded wooden frame.

Use restrained aged-gold leaf, shallow floral and scroll carving, narrow inner beading, slight irregular wear, and believable depth.

The frame is part of the artwork, not a digital border.

Compared with CUT 01, the frame carving may be slightly simpler so the bride remains more visually concentrated.

## 7) MODERN BRIDAL GOWN

Yulim wears a warm-ivory silk-satin modern couture bridal gown.

Use an elegant square-to-soft-scoop neckline, structured bodice with hidden couture corsetry, natural-to-slightly-defined waist, and a refined long skirt whose train continues beyond the tighter crop.

Use clean sleeveless construction or refined cap sleeves.
Apply only low-density pearl embroidery or subtle lace appliqué.

The gown must remain modern bridal couture rather than historical costume.

### Bust Volume and Construction Lock

Render Yulim with a visibly fuller, softly rounded, naturally supported feminine bust using realistic adult anatomy.

The volume must be expressed through the external silhouette of the fitted silk bodice, hidden internal cup support, couture corsetry, and believable fabric tension.

The square-to-soft-scoop neckline is structurally locked.
Its height, width, depth, corners, and shoulder attachment must remain unchanged.

Do not lower the neckline.
Do not widen it.
Do not turn it into a sweetheart, plunging, balconette, strapless, or exposed-corset design.

The bust must remain fully contained inside the gown.
The silk follows the rounded chest with controlled natural tension and smooth painted highlights.

No breast spill.
No extreme push-up shelf.
No visible bra outline.
No sheer panel.
No nipple detail.
No deformed cup shape.
No broken neckline corners.

The result should be fuller and elegant, but fully dressed and sophisticated.

## 8) COMPOSITION · STANDING POSE

Vertical 3:4.

Standing knee-up or half-length painted portrait.

This composition is noticeably tighter than CUT 01 and more focused on the bride.

Use a near eye-level viewpoint.
Place Yulim close to the visual center but not mechanically centered.

Turn her torso approximately 25–30 degrees from frontal.
Turn her face back toward the viewer.
Let one shoulder sit fractionally farther back.
Spine upright.
Chin slightly lowered.

Both hands meet naturally below the waist.
One hand rests lightly over the back of the other.
Fingers remain individually readable and naturally separated.
Wrists aligned.

Do not interlace fingers tightly.

## 9) GAZE · EXPRESSION

Use direct or almost-direct viewer gaze.

The expression is quiet, inward, noble, and gently personal without melancholy.

Upper eyelids comfortably open.
Brows relaxed.
Glabella relaxed.
Jaw released.

Lips softly closed or separated by less than 1 mm.
Only the smallest suggestion of warmth appears at the corners.

No broad smile.

## 10) MAKEUP — PAINTED BRIDAL ROSE

Apply refined Classic Rose bridal styling only as painted surface color and tonal placement.

Use a neutral soft-satin complexion translated through delicate oil glazing.
Preserve subtle natural variation around the eyes, nose, cheeks, and lips.

Use muted rose-taupe eyelid modeling within the actual eye anatomy.
Keep lash definition restrained.
Paint softly defined brows.
Diffuse dried-rose blush through soft transitions.
Use a muted rose lip with a very restrained painted highlight following the real lip curvature.

Do not alter eye size, nose size, lip size, jaw shape, or facial proportions.

## 11) LIGHTING

Use one soft natural window source approximately 45 degrees to one side and slightly above Yulim.

Create controlled painted highlights on:
forehead,
upper cheek,
nose bridge,
eyelids,
lip curvature,
hair edge,
neckline,
upper bust surface of the silk bodice,
hands,
and selected gown folds.

Use warm-neutral interior bounce on the shadow side.

The face must remain fully readable, but the lighting must support painterly modeling rather than photographic skin realism.

## 12) ESSENTIAL PAINTERLY CORRECTION

This prompt must strongly avoid the “painted image with still-photographic face” problem.

The bride’s face must be unmistakably oil-painted even when enlarged.

When zoomed in, the face should still show:
soft brush-led contour transitions,
painted eyelid and under-eye modeling,
readable but painterly eyes,
painted brow texture,
non-photographic lip edges,
and unified oil-painted skin structure.

The final result must feel like a real oil portrait of Yulim, not a retouched photograph converted into a painting style.

## 13) PHYSICAL AND STRUCTURAL ANCHORS

Yulim’s face is the absolute first priority.

Her bridal hair, neckline, fuller-bust silhouette, and hands form the secondary visual rhythm.

Maintain coherent standing balance, correct shoulder alignment, believable gown drape, natural train fall, realistic hand overlap, and anatomically sound fingers.

Everything remains painterly but structurally accurate.

## 14) WATERMARK

If watermark inclusion is required, place a very small subtle “ⓒyulim_mood” at the extreme bottom-right corner, visually subordinate to the antique frame.

## 15) NEGATIVE PROMPT

tight interlaced hands, fused fingers, extra fingers, malformed wrists,
crop copied from CUT 01, visible groom, chair,

MANDATORY HAIR REPLACEMENT.

Replace the hairstyle visible in the reference image completely.

Use naturally dark black-brown hair, smoothly gathered with a nearly centered clean part and no bangs. Keep the forehead, temples, and ears neatly open. Gather all hair into a small, compact, historically restrained low jjok-style bun positioned immediately above the nape.

Keep crown volume low and natural. Do not use loose modern face-framing curls.

Insert one narrow aged-brass or dark-silver binyeo horizontally through the bun.

Do not retain the source hairstyle’s length, outer silhouette, curl pattern, bangs, parting, loose structure, modern layering, high bun, C-curls, S-waves, see-through bangs, or modern volume.

The final silhouette must be low, compact, practical, restrained, and historically plausible.

Change only the hair while preserving Yulim’s exact recognizable facial identity.

## 2) FILM CHARACTER

Photographed on Kodak Portra 400 using a full-frame 35mm photographic workflow.

Use the tonal behavior of Portra 400: soft warm skin, muted saturation, gentle highlight roll-off, restrained contrast, creamy ivory reproduction, subdued celadon greens, warm walnut browns, subtle organic grain, and readable shadow detail.

Avoid artificial HDR, harsh digital micro-contrast, over-saturation, crispy sharpening, and synthetic cinematic grading.

## 3) SCENE CONCEPT AND STORY

Portray Jang Gye-hyang at the moment she begins translating practical cooking knowledge into written language.

Narrative: “Hands that already know the taste begin to leave it in words.”

The image must not look like a ceremonial historical portrait or a posed calligraphy demonstration. She is actually writing something useful from lived experience.

Yulim’s tactile persona appears through the contact between fingertips, brush shaft, wet ink, handmade hanji, silk-hemp fabric, and worn wood.

## 4) LOCATION · TIME · ENVIRONMENT

A small writing room opening onto the edge of a raised wooden toenmaru inside a Joseon-period scholar household.

Early autumn, approximately 09:10 in the morning.

Soft daylight passes through traditional hanji-covered doors. The room is calm and moderately bright, not dramatically dark. The morning air feels clear, dry, and mildly warm.

## 5) BACKGROUND AND PROPS

Foreground: a softly out-of-focus corner of an inkstone and one spare brush lying diagonally.

Midground: Yulim seated at a low wooden writing desk, one sheet of handmade hanji, a small inkstone containing wet black ink, and the active brush.

Background: a partially opened paper door, the wooden toenmaru, a quiet courtyard, and one or two sunlit earthenware jars.

The hanji must show fine fibers, tiny undulations, irregular edges, and slight curling. The writing desk has subdued grain, small wear marks, and believable age. Wet ink visibly absorbs into the paper with slightly softened edges.

Avoid generic Chinese architecture, Japanese interiors, fantasy palace objects, excessive pottery, and museum-display styling.

## 6) WARDROBE AND BODY SILHOUETTE

Dress Yulim in a historically restrained mid-Joseon-inspired noblewoman’s hanbok.

The jeogori is warm ivory to pale oatmeal, made from a fine natural silk-and-ramie-like woven textile with restrained visible fiber texture. It has sufficient historical length and natural ease through the torso rather than a short contemporary silhouette.

Use a clean soft-cream collar and muted celadon-green goreum. The sleeves are moderately generous at the wrist and form deep irregular folds as the elbows bend.

The chima is dusty jade to muted celadon, made from substantial low-luster silk. It falls with unequal vertical folds and naturally compresses beneath the seated pelvis, legs, and knees.

Give Yulim a naturally full, mature feminine bust with realistic adult anatomy and clearly readable chest volume.

IMPORTANT: Do not make the jeogori tight, cropped, elastic, corseted, low-cut, transparent, bodycon, or shaped like a modern blouse.

The fuller bust must appear through natural three-dimensional body volume beneath a correctly loose historical jeogori. Maintain adequate fabric ease across the chest while allowing subtle outward volume, realistic gravity, soft tension transitions, and natural folds beneath and beside the bust.

No exposed cleavage. No exaggerated individual breast outlines through the fabric. No distorted goreum. No modern push-up or corset silhouette.

## 7) MAKEUP AND SKIN

Use cinematic no-makeup makeup.

Apply a very thin warm-neutral skin tint that preserves realistic pores, fine natural vellus hair, subtle tonal variation, and natural color around the eyes, nose, cheeks, and lips. Maintain soft matte-to-satin skin variation.

Keep natural eyebrow hairs visible with minimal grooming. Use nearly invisible beige-taupe eyelid shading. No visible eyeliner. Natural separated lashes without exaggerated length. A very faint rose-beige flush on the cheeks. Natural muted-rose tinted lip balm with preserved natural lip shape, asymmetry, and texture.

Do not alter facial anatomy through makeup.

## 8) CAMERA AND COMPOSITION

Vertical 3:4. Full-frame camera, 65mm lens, f/2.8. Waist-up medium portrait.

Camera height approximately 120cm. Place the camera above and to Yulim’s right, using an oblique downward angle of approximately 68–74 degrees while keeping her face fully readable.

Her torso is oriented approximately 35 degrees relative to the desk. Her right shoulder is slightly forward. The upper body inclines only about 10 degrees toward the writing surface.

No direct camera gaze. Her eyes are focused between the brush tip and the freshly written line.

Keep both eyes, eyebrows, nose bridge, lips, and jaw transition sufficiently readable within the focal plane.

## 9) HANDS AND PHYSICAL CONTACT

Her right thumb, index finger, and middle finger control the brush shaft with believable writing pressure. Ring finger and little finger remain naturally curved and separated.

The brush tip physically touches the paper. Her left index and middle-finger side surfaces gently stabilize the lower corner of the hanji. Do not overlap the two hands.

Show small realistic contact shadows beneath the fingertips. The brush hairs compress slightly against the paper. Wet ink softly absorbs into the fibers. Her right sleeve touches the writing-desk edge and compresses naturally against the wood.

## 10) MODEL EXPRESSION

Use Yulim’s warm, quiet, tactile emotional language.

Upper eyelids gently lowered in concentration. Brows relaxed. No tension between the eyebrows. Lips softly closed with minimal pressure. Jaw and cheeks released.

No camera smile. No exaggerated scholarly severity. She appears absorbed in the physical act of writing.

Maintain the target hair: low compact black-brown jjok bun immediately above the nape, nearly centered part, no bangs, low crown volume, one understated aged-metal binyeo.

## 11) LIGHTING

Use a large soft natural key from the front-left hanji door. The hanji manuscript provides a subtle warm-ivory upward fill. The wooden wall on camera-right adds soft brown bounce.

A delicate natural rim touches the hair edge, part of the jawline, and right shoulder. Catchlights must correspond to the large paper-window source.

Preserve highlight detail in the ivory jeogori and readable texture on the shadow side of the face.

## 12) ESSENTIAL PHYSICAL ANCHORS

The attached reference remains the sole facial identity throughout the image. Replace the reference hairstyle completely with the specified historical low jjok.

Prioritize real writing over a staged historical pose. Maintain believable wet ink absorption, brush-tip deformation, paper fibers, finger pressure, sleeve compression, fabric gravity, chest-to-garment volume, contact shadows, coherent perspective, and progressive optical depth.

The fuller bust must remain naturally contained within a structurally correct loose historical jeogori.

## 13) WATERMARK
